what_it_does: Running a very large AI language model (70 billion parameters or more) is limited not by raw computation but by how fast the hardware can load the model's weights from memory — memory bandwidth is the bottleneck. One solution called PIM (processing-in-memory — doing math right inside the memory chip rather than shipping data to a separate processor) can help, but a single large memory die cannot hold the full model. McPAL stacks multiple smaller memory-with-compute chips together in two ways: vertically (layers bonded on top of each other, like a short stack of pancakes, using a technology called 3D-HBM — high-bandwidth memory stacked in 3D) to reduce how far data travels, and horizontally (multiple stacks connected via a 2D interposer chip) to reach the total capacity needed for 70B+ models. The system also handles unstructured sparsity (the model's weights where many values are zero or near-zero and can be skipped), routing only the non-skipped computations through a butterfly-shaped interconnect inside the memory to keep the compute units busy.
